sources.entry: Universal Exam Cram Coach by ZeKai Nie - A multimodal, grounded active-learning tutor engine for college textbooks. Mitigates AI hallucinations and diagram blindness with automated vector figure cropping, homework-solution auto-pairing, and cross-session persistent state. Benchmarked on STEM courseware to run on small models with significant token savings.

summary.one_liner: An AI exam-prep tutor Agent Skill (with a small offline Python CLI) that turns your course slides, notes, homework and past papers into chapter-by-chapter teaching, page-cited quizzes and a mistake log.
summary.what_it_does: The skill reads PDF, PPTX, DOCX, Markdown, TXT, HTML and image files from a materials folder and splits the course into chapters, using file-name numbers or "Chapter N" headings. It extracts questions and pairs them with their reference solutions (for example hw2.pdf with hw2solutions.pdf, or textbook labels like "Problem 1.3.10"). It crops figures from PDF, PPTX and DOCX files with pypdfium2 so the agent can show them while explaining. Each taught sentence is labelled as coming from the materials, as AI supplement, or as an AI-generated answer, with file and page citations. State such as progress, quiz results, mistakes and notes is kept in a local study_state.json and a workspace folder, so a session can resume later. The command-line tool provides commands for setup, next slice, quiz, grading of choice and short answers, ask/search, mistakes, cheat sheet, and a day-by-day plan to the exam date. The README reports measured setup times and tests with small models such as Gemini Flash-Lite and Claude Haiku.
use_cases: prepare for a final or midterm from lecture slides and notes
quiz yourself using homework and past exam questions
get chapter-by-chapter explanations with page citations
track mistakes and review them before an exam
build a cheat sheet from course notes
plan daily study sessions until an exam date
resume a study session across chats
how_to_run: Tell your agent: Use the Exam Cram Coach skill. My materials are in <folder>. The exam is in 3 days; teach me from chapter 1.
stack: pypdfium2 (optional, PDF text and figure cropping)
notable: Figure cropping: automatically cuts vector drawings and embedded images from lecture PDFs, slides and documents, and attaches answer figures to quiz items
Homework-solution auto-pairing by base file name and textbook problem labels
Provenance labels (🟢 from materials, 🟡 AI supplement, ⚠️ AI-generated answer) on every taught sentence
Local persistent state in study_state.json, resumable across chat sessions without a vector database
Two editions: lightweight Flash (this root skill) and a full v4.3 edition in full/ with HTML/PDF study guides
caveats: Terminals often cannot display figures; desktop or IDE versions of agents are recommended for PDF-heavy courses
Scanned or handwritten pages are detected and skipped, not used as content
Excel files and audio are not read
Textbook problems without statements in the folder show only the reference solution's givens
The README's benchmarks were measured on the author's own machine and courses, and the MIT and Yale sample courses are CC BY-NC-SA
